messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — Elevated end-to-end latency and streaming stalls detected in us-west-2 serving plane. p95 ~ 920ms, p99 spikes > 6s, streaming stall rate climbed from 0.5% to ~8%. Paging on-call: @owen

owen: on-call ack. grabbing dashboards now. who has customer impact list? @jordan can you standby for comms?

maya: metrics snapshot: spike started 2026-03-14T12:13:40Z. TLS handshake failures up 4x, DNS resolution times erratic (100ms -> 1.3s). Initial traceroutes show an extra hop with 100-200ms jitter crossing AZs.

alex: looking at VPC flow logs and our nat-proxy telemetry — high retransmit counts and connection queueing on nat-proxy instances in us-west-2b. ASG hit desired capacity around the start of the spike. Also seeing interface drops.

owen: immediate mitigations proposal: 1) force AZ-local egress for streaming sessions, 2) temporarily limit new connection creation rate on frontends to prefer reuse, 3) scale nat-proxy fleet + change scaling policy to be more aggressive. execute quickly.

eng-ops: deploying egress-local policy as a progressive rollout (10% -> 50% -> 75%). Will also bump nat-proxy ASG by +40% now.

maya: canary at 10% shows p99 drop from ~6.5s -> 1.2s, stalls down to 2% in canary. Non-canary remains degraded. Good signal.

alex: nat-proxy logs showing SYN retransmits; sample tcpdump below. Also routing change frequency indicates potential transient route flaps via the cross-AZ transit path.

```
12:14:02.234567 IP frontend -> nat-proxy: Flags [S], seq 0
12:14:03.078901 IP frontend -> nat-proxy: Flags [S], seq 0 (retransmit)
12:14:05.341210 IP nat-proxy -> external: Flags [S], seq 0
```

# traceroute excerpt
```
1 10.0.40.1 0.56 ms
2 10.0.16.254 1.05 ms
3 52.92.11.202 8.94 ms
4 34.210.99.1 180.12 ms  <-- cross-AZ jitter
```

owen: actioned: nat-proxy ASG desired +40%, egress-local routing up to 50% traffic, enabled frontend keepalive tuning (keepalive_requests 5000, keepalive_timeout 75s), added local DNS caching layer on frontends.

incident-bot: routing change at 12:19:10Z propagated to ~50% of us-west-2. Monitoring window 15m.

riley: I'm taking the next rotation in 25m. Please summarise the handoff state.

jordan: CS update — drafting initial customer notice for impacted tenants. Roughly 2.5% of hosted traffic experienced degraded streaming; one enterprise customer reported repeated reconnects. Will queue follow-up when we have ETA.

maya: digging deeper on DNS — queries routed across AZ resolved slower when forced through cross-AZ NAT. Implemented iptables rule to pin DNS to same-AZ resolver and started local nscd cache.

alex: verified new nat-proxy instances came up healthy. However, scaling lag means some of the earlier queues caused tail latencies. We'll need faster autoscale triggers or reserved capacity.

owen: handoff summary for riley:
- start_ts: 1789004321 (12:13:40Z)
- symptoms: p99 tail >6s, streaming stalls ~8%, TLS handshake timeouts, DNS tail latency
- suspected causes: nat-proxy/NAT saturation + cross-AZ packet loss/jitter + DNS routing across AZs
- mitigations applied: AZ-local egress rollout (50%), nat-proxy ASG +40%, frontend keepalive tuning, DNS pinning + local caching
- customer impact: ~2.5% hosted API requests affected; streaming retries observed for some dedicated connections
- owners: alex (network eng) for NAT scaling and infra, maya (SRE) for frontend and DNS caching, riley (oncall) for monitoring and customer comms

riley: got it. I'll watch metrics for 2 hours. If p99 < 1.5s and stall rate < 1% for 20 consecutive minutes, we can start rolling back temporary routing. ETA to full mitigation depends on infra changes (~2-5 hours).

eng-ops: nat-proxy ASG scaled new instances; health checks passed. Canary traffic shows stable latencies. No new error spikes in the scaled group.

jordan: initial customer notice sent. One customer asked for timeline; provided ETA 2-5h and promised RCA later.

maya: collected packet captures and uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/1789004321/pcap_bundle.tar.gz. Logging snapshots also stored under the incident ticket.

owen: post-incident actions to include in postmortem:
- alex: review nat-proxy ASG scaling thresholds, improve responsiveness and consider reserved instances for peak windows
- eng-ops: implement auto-fallback to AZ-local egress when cross-AZ retransmit rate > 0.8%
- maya: bake in local DNS caching and increase default keepalive reuse in frontend images
- riley: draft incident timeline and customer impact severity

incident-bot: Incident record created: INC-2028-1789004321. Severity set to Sev2. Pager rotation updated.

riley: ending active page. Will reopen if regressions. Thank you all for the fast response :thumbsup:

owen: great work. Please attach postmortem owners to the ticket and loop me in for review before publishing.
